newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel says vehicle registrations up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Opel says vehicle registrations up in 1996.

text.p: Adam Opel AG, the German unit of U.S. carmaker General Motors Corp, said on Tuesday that vehicle registrations of its models rose to 568,000 in 1996 from 565,000 in 1995, the highest level since 1992.

Opel said all models contributed to the slightly higher sales and that its Opel and Vauxhall brands continued to be the leaders in western Europe for the fifth consecutive year with a total market share of 12 percent.
But Opel said its German market share slipped to 16.2 percent in 1996 from about 17 percent in 1995, in part due to stiffer competition.
On a European basis, GM said the Opel and Vauxhall brands had sales of 1.54 million units, a 2.1 percent increase over 1995 levels, in an overall market of 12.8 million vehicles.
Total GM group sales, including Swedish carmaker Saab in which GM has a 50 percent stake, and GM-made cars from the U.S. sold in Europe, reached 1.61 million units for a market share of 12.5 percent.
Opel said it set all-time high market shares in France, Italy, Poland, the Czech and Slovak Republics and in Turkey.
GM also said Opel and Vauxhall production plants in Europe set a new production record of 1.84 million vehicles and component sets, up 2.5 percent over 1995 levels.
